QUANTUM SENSING WITHOUT CALIBRATING THE NOISE AXIS
A finite controller based on returning error trajectories
1 November 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

Research status
===============
This investigation derives a physical-model construction, ordinary proofs, and
independent executable checks. Historical novelty, laboratory realization, and
practical superiority over the strongest conventional methods are unestablished.
The main result includes continuing sensor noise during finite meter interaction,
feedback latency, readout and reset. It allows constant classical report errors.
Protected reference memory, specified coherent interactions, and a shared static
native noise axis remain material premises. Generic quantum controller faults
are separately charged; this is not a fault-tolerance threshold theorem.

The initial scientific objective was a quantum sensor whose improving precision
does not demand equally improving knowledge of an environmental noise direction.
The strongest ordinary known-noise QEC constructions were considered first.
Their failure with a nuisance noise direction identified the opening. The useful
result changes the physical operation set by allowing scalar reservoir-rate
control. That operation is neither free information nor an ordinary Pauli pulse.

1. Task and exact physical contract
==================================
There is one sensing qubit S with unknown frequency omega and one protected
reference qubit A. Z|0>=|0>, Z|1>=-|1>. Encode a logical qubit by

    |0_L>=|0_S 0_A>,    |1_L>=|1_S 1_A>.

Its input can be unknown and entangled with an arbitrary untouched reference R.
For the final sensing task the input is |+_L>. The sensor has Hamiltonian
H_omega=omega Z_S/2 and Markov noise

    L_theta=sqrt(gamma) J_theta,
    J_theta=cos(theta) X_S+sin(theta) Y_S.

The azimuth theta is unknown, constant, and common to every native-rate setting.
Two strictly positive rates gamma_l<gamma_h can be selected. The physical control
changes only this scalar coefficient. It does not turn off the noise, resolve
theta, add an independently oriented noise source, or alter H_omega. A microscopic
resource consistent with this contract is a tunable scalar coupling to one fixed
system operator J_theta and a sufficiently broad stationary Markov reservoir.

# A finite two-body meter for feedback-controlled error return

Construction and independent audit, 1 November 2026.

## Purpose

The root investigation proposes storing a sensing qubit in |0_L>=|00>, |1_L>=|11>, allowing sensor jumps J_theta=cos(theta)X+sin(theta)Y to move between even and odd parity, and controlling the scalar jump rate based on imperfect parity information. There is no X correction on the data. Every even total jump history has J_theta factors cancel exactly; theta remains only in odd final parity, which can be erased or removed from the sensing observable.

The challenge is to acquire parity information during continuing sensor noise without a fictitious instantaneous parity oracle or a three-body parity coupling.

## Explicit finite two-body Hamiltonian

Let s be the sensor, a the noiseless reference ancilla, and m a fresh meter initialized in |0>_m. During a finite interval tau use

    H = omega Z_s/2 + g_s Z_s X_m + g_a Z_a X_m,
    L_theta = sqrt(gamma) J_theta,s.

The two interactions Z_s X_m and Z_a X_m each involve only two qubits. They commute. Their amplitudes are constant during one interval; switching scalar gamma occurs between intervals based on the previous meter outcome.

For a particular sensor jump history, let r(t)=+1 in even parity and -1 in odd parity, and write z=+1/-1 for the ancilla Z eigenvalue, which labels the logical computational basis. Then Z_s(t)=z r(t), while Z_a=z throughout. Put

    Y = integral_0^tau r(t) dt,
    Phi = g_a tau + g_s Y.

The meter evolution on that logical component is exactly exp(-i z Phi X_m), including jumps during the readout interaction. The signal accumulates exp(-i omega z Y/2).

A final Z_m measurement produces scalar cos(Phi) for outcome 0 or -i z sin(Phi) for outcome 1. With a perfectly reported meter outcome, track a known Z_a frame on outcome 1. Then the meter's action is a scalar on the unknown logical state for EVERY jump history. No logical value has leaked into the retained measurement record. This holds on arbitrary logical-reference inputs. The coherent-erasure extension below removes the assumption that the classical outcome is reported perfectly.

The correction is a software sign frame: Z_a commutes with the signal, sensor jumps, and all subsequent meter interactions. No physical data correction gate is required.

Statistical audit of syndrome-dependent native-noise feedback
1 November 2026; independent complementary construction

Scope. The parent construction now uses a finite physical meter with ongoing
sensor noise, coherent removal of logical information from the meter, and a
feedback choice between two scalar native noise rates. This note audits the
information claim and preserves an exactly solved simpler instantaneous weak-
parity instrument as a reference. It does not claim a device demonstration or
historical novelty.

1. Pathwise statement and the correct achievable information

Take H=omega Z_P/2 and jumps A_theta=cos(theta)X_P+sin(theta)Y_P, with fixed but
unknown theta. Encode |0_L>=|00>, |1_L>=|11>. No physical correction flips are
applied. Let S(t)=+1 in the even sector and -1 in the odd sector, with S(0)=+1,
and A_T=integral_0^T S(t)dt. All logical-safe measurement/control amplitudes
must be scalar in the logical bit conditional on a syndrome path.

For every path ending in the even sector, the product of unknown A_theta
jumps has no remaining theta dependence. Its logical unitary is
exp(-i omega A_T Z_L/2), up to a known convention on the sign of A_T.
This follows from A_theta^2=I and A_theta exp(-i x Z/2) A_theta=exp(+i x Z/2).
The assertion holds for an arbitrary logical state and reference system.

Unobserved paths are still mixed. Define
  p_e(T)=P(S(T)=+1),
  M(T)=E[A_T 1{S(T)=+1}].
If an ideal final measurement resolves even Y_L and odd erasure, its actually
achieved Fisher information at omega=0 is
  I_omega(0)=M(T)^2/p_e(T).
It is NOT E[A_T^2 1_even], since the unknown residence time is not revealed.

The parent now avoids perfect final parity altogether. The observable
  O=(X_P Y_A + Y_P X_A)/2
equals Y_L in the even sector and zero in the odd sector. Choose either product
Pauli measurement with probability 1/2, and keep only its product outcome z=+/-1.
Then P(z)= [1+z f_T(omega)]/2, where
  f_T(omega)=E[1_even sin(omega A_T)]
up to an overall known sign. This entire binary distribution is theta-independent.
At omega=0, f_T=0 and f_T'=M(T), so the achieved classical FI is exactly M(T)^2.
When p_e -> pi_e and M(T)/T -> pi_e v>0, this yields
  I_omega(0)/T^2 -> pi_e^2 v^2.
No quantum Fi
